This is a fluff piece. Auto insurance profits (and personal insurance policies in general) have been sliced razor thin by the competition between the major players in the industry. In addition, if premiums fall by 60% but claims fall by more than 60%, the auto industry is going to be doing better, not worse (though they'll have less benefit from float, which is really where all the money is made anyway).

The reality is that uncertainty (any uncertainty) in a market is good for insurance companies, because it generally means that premiums (thus profits) go up. I would put good money on a surcharge being added to the premiums of every auto policy in the first few states that have self-driving cars on the road.

Ok, but if a lot of drivers let's say 60% drive an autonomous auto then the type of insurance that these people would get would be pretty much the same, the insurance companies would sell the same product.
